title: `gc sling <target> <bead> --on <v2-formula>` does not stamp `gc.source_bead_id`, so workflow-finalize cannot close the source bead
body:
## Environment

- gascity edge (post-1.3.3), source snapshot `8b17c64`
- macOS (darwin/arm64), `gc` built from source
- `GC_BEADS=file` (observed there; the code path is backend-independent)

## Summary

Attaching a **formulas-v2 (graph) formula** to an existing bead with
`gc sling <target> <bead-id> --on <formula>` launches the workflow, but the
workflow root never receives `gc.source_bead_id`. As a result, when the
workflow finalizes with outcome pass, `closeSourceBeadChain` finds no source
metadata and stops as a no-op — the source bead the formula was attached to
stays open forever and must be closed by hand.

The legacy (non-graph) `--on` path stamps the source correctly; only the v2
graph branch drops it.

## Minimal repro

1. Create a city with a v2 formula (any `version = 2` graph formula) and one
   agent that can run it.
2. `bd create` (or `gc bd create`) a work bead; note its id, e.g. `gc-101`.
3. `gc sling <agent> gc-101 --on <v2-formula>` — the workflow instantiates and
   starts.
4. Inspect the workflow root bead's metadata.
5. Let the workflow run to completion (all steps pass, `workflow-finalize`
   fires).

**Observed:** the root has no `gc.source_bead_id` (step 4); after finalize the
root closes but `gc-101` remains open (step 5). The finalize trace logs
`close-source-chain ... stop reason=no_source`.

**Expected:** the root carries `gc.source_bead_id=gc-101` and finalize closes
`gc-101` along with the root, as the non-graph `--on` path does.

title: bug: gc init fails to detect Gemini CLI installed via Nix (does not respect $PATH)
body:
### Before you continue

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I read the relevant docs and contributor guidance.

### Gas City version

1.3.3

### Environment

macosx , gc installed via nix

### Reproduction


 1. Install the gemini-cli using Nix.
 2. Verify the gemini binary is available in $PATH and executable:
    ```bash
      $ which gemini
      /Users/username/.nix-profile/bin/gemini

      $ gemini --version
      0.47.0
    ```
 3. Run gc init with Gemini as the provider:
    ```bash
      $ gc init --default-provider gemini
      gc init: provider readiness preflight failed: Gemini CLI: is not installed
    ```

### Expected behavior


 gascity should fall back to checking $PATH (e.g., using exec.LookPath("gemini")) if the binary isn't found in standard npm directories, or prioritize $PATH entirely.

### Actual behavior

gc init: provider readiness preflight failed: Gemini CLI: is not installed

### Logs, screenshots, or traces

```shell

```

### Additional context

When the gemini CLI is installed via Nix and is fully accessible in the system $PATH, gc init --default-provider gemini fails with a "not installed" error.

 It appears that gascity explicitly checks hardcoded npm global installation paths (such as ~/.npm-global/bin) to find the CLI, rather than resolving the binary using the user's
 $PATH.

title: bug: orders: never-run cron order can't bootstrap — catch-up scan skipped when lastRun is zero (residual gap in #2721)
body:
## Summary

A cron order that has **never fired** can never bootstrap: `checkCron`'s catch-up scan (added by #2721 to fix exactly this class of miss) is skipped when `lastRun` is zero, so a freshly-installed narrow-window order (single minute/day) is left depending on the exact-minute luck that #2721 was written to eliminate. If its first scheduled minute never coincides with a controller evaluation, it fires never — and no restart helps, because `lastRun` stays zero.

## Symptom

A daily-once cron order installed and enabled, with correct config, accumulates **zero** order history and silently never fires. `gc order check` shows `cron: schedule not matched` at all times. Unlike #2599 (warm orders that drop after multi-day uptime and recover on supervisor restart), a restart does **not** help here — there is no prior `lastRun` to recover to.

Observed 2026-07-05 on `janitor-worktree-gc` (`schedule = "20 4 * * *"`), installed 2026-07-04:

- Missed both of its first two 04:20 windows (07-04 and 07-05).

title: bug: gc formula cook --attach drops rig context, making rig-scoped graph.v2 targets unresolvable
body:
### Summary

`gc formula cook --attach` on a graph.v2 formula drops the invocation's **rig context** at the decorate step, so rig-scoped step targets that are **not city-unique** fail to resolve. `gc sling` on the same formula works, because it passes a real rig context. The failure looks intermittent because it only bites *bare* rig-scoped names present under more than one rig.

### Environment

- Gas City **v1.3.3** (`55acb48`); also reproduced against current **`main`** (buggy function is byte-identical).
- Linux, Go 1.26. A multi-rig city where an imported pack contributes the same agent bare-name to more than one rig.

### Reproduction

1. A city with ≥2 rigs (e.g. `dip`, `ce`), each importing a pack that provides an agent under the same bare name (e.g. `run-operator`) — so the bare name is not city-unique.
2. A graph.v2 formula whose steps route to that bare rig-scoped target.
3. Run `gc formula cook --attach=<bead-id> <formula>` from within the rig.

**Expected:** the step resolves to `dip/run-operator` (the invocation's rig context) — exactly as `gc sling <that-formula>` does.

**Actual:** `decorate formulas v2 recipe: step <id>: unknown formulas v2 target "run-operator"`.

### Root cause

`decorateFormulaCookGraphV2Recipe` (`cmd/gc/cmd_formula.go:888-889`) calls:

```go
graphroute.DecorateGraphWorkflowRecipe(recipe, ..., /*routedTo*/ "", /*sessionName*/ "", ...)
```

`mol-witness-patrol`'s own wisp-reconciliation commands (added in #3243 to fix

title: Feature: a --no-supervisor / isolated-start mode for gc start (safe cutover gating beside a live supervisor)
body:
## Problem

Gating a migration/cutover that involves `gc start` (e.g. a beads backend swap) is hard on a host that already runs a live city, because `gc start` registers with the **machine-wide supervisor** — and the `127.0.0.1:8372` bind is effectively an unrelocatable singleton:

- `[api]` port config, `$GCH`, and `~/.gc/supervisor.toml` are ignored for the bind;
- `GC_NO_API` doesn't stop it;
- rootless network-namespace isolation fails (`uid_map` EPERM) without privilege.

So a second full `gc start` — even on a throwaway clone with an isolated `GC_HOME` — collides with the live supervisor or is fatal. There is no supported way to exercise the real `gc start` path in isolation next to a live convoy.

## Impact

Operators gating a cutover must fall back to *proxies* (`gc start --dry-run`, an isolated `gc import install`) or run the real start fully detached against the live city with auto-rollback. Workable, but it leaves a gap: **no clean, supervisor-free way to rehearse a full start on a copy before touching production** — which is exactly the path that historically breaks cutovers.

## Ask

A `--no-supervisor` (or `--isolated`, or `GC_SUPERVISOR=none`) mode for `gc start` that:

- runs the start's reconcile/init path against a given `GC_HOME` + city **without** binding the machine supervisor port or registering with the live controller, and
- exits after the start-equivalent work (or runs a one-shot foreground controller on an ephemeral / overridable port).

title: cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close: at-most-once dedup counts a queued nudge as delivered — a dead-lettered nudge permanently swallows the dependent's wake-up
body:
## Summary

The `cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close` order's at-most-once dedup can permanently swallow a wake-up: a `(blocker, dependent)` pair is marked "nudged" the moment `gc session nudge` returns success — but in the default `wait-idle` mode, "success" includes "queued." If that queued nudge later dead-letters, the cascade never re-nudges the pair, and the dependent's assignee gets no signal that their work is unblocked until the dedup entry ages out (default 1 hour) — or ever, if nothing else wakes them.

Split out from the profiling findings in #3924 (item 2) because it's a correctness hazard, not a performance observation.

## Mechanism

1. A blocker closes; on a later controller tick the order script runs and calls `gc session nudge <assignee> …` for each open, assigned dependent (`internal/bootstrap/packs/core/assets/scripts/cascade-nudge-on-blocker-close.sh:109-130`).
2. The script records the `(blocker|dependent)` dedup key **whenever the nudge command exits 0** (`.sh:130-131`).
3. `gc session nudge` defaults to `wait-idle` (`cmd/gc/cmd_session.go:2374`). On a busy/managed-but-not-running session it **queues** the nudge and reports success (`cmd/gc/cmd_nudge.go:720-748`, fall-through to queue at `:778-780`).
4. The queued item can dead-letter: `defaultQueuedNudgeMaxAttempts = 5`, retry delay 15 s, TTL 24 h, claim lease 2 m (`cmd/gc/cmd_nudge.go:37-41`). Delivery failures (session gone, provider stall, repeated non-idle) exhaust attempts.

title: No session lifecycle events in the events stream — readiness tooling is forced to poll; relates to #2895 (start-pending wedges)
body:
**Environment:** gc 1.3.2, macOS arm64, supervisor-managed city.

**Problem.** The events log carries rich `bead.*`/`order.*`/`convoy.*` types — `gc events --watch --type convoy.closed` blocks and fires beautifully — but **zero `session.*` types** (checked over multi-hour windows at both city and supervisor scope, spanning several session creations, starts, and sleeps). `gc analyze reliability` itself reports lifecycle instrumentation gaps ("no worker.operation observed").

**Why it matters:** any tooling that must wait for a session to come up (we escort a human's tmux client into freshly spawned interactive sessions) has no event to watch — it polls `tmux has-session` or `gc session list --json` on a timer sized to worst-case reconciler latency. When a spawn wedges in `start-pending` (#2895 — we've reproduced it twice; `gc session wake` cleared it both times in ~40s), polling can't distinguish "slow" from "wedged, will never arrive."

**Asks:** (a) emit session lifecycle events (created / starting / ready / failed) to the events stream so readiness is watchable like convoys are; (b) time-box `start-pending` (retry or fail loudly) rather than wedging silently — complements #2895's TTL-reap proposal; (c) document pin-vs-wake start semantics (pin supplies a run-reason but we've observed pin alone never enqueue the start; wake cleared it).

title: builtin:claude hardcodes `--effort max` and it cannot be overridden (agent `args` are prepended + last-flag-wins; settings-file `effort` is overridden by the flag); agent `model` key silently dropped
body:
**Environment:** gc 1.3.2, claude CLI harness, macOS arm64.

**Problem.** Every claude session is spawned `claude … --effort max --settings <city>/.gc/settings.json`. The flag appears in no config surface (city.toml, provider block, pack, resolved `gc config show`) — it is baked into the builtin:claude provider. For orchestration-only agents (routers/front-desks) this burns maximum-depth reasoning on every turn: we measured **40–56s of model time per trivial status turn** that drops to seconds at lower effort.

**Both adopter override paths are defeated (verified behaviorally):**
- **Agent-level `args`** (accepted key in `agents/<name>/agent.toml`) is **prepended**, producing `claude --effort medium … --effort max …`. The claude CLI is last-flag-wins — proven by thinking-token spread on a fixed reasoning prompt: `--effort low`=49 output tokens, `--effort max`=375; `low` then `max`=294 (≈max wins), `max` then `low`=20 (≈low wins). So the builtin's flag always wins.
- The **settings file honors an `effort` key** (settings-low alone → 45 tokens) but the CLI flag overrides it (settings-low + `--effort max` → 206 ≈ max).

**Related footgun:** an agent-level `model` key in agent.toml is **silently dropped** — no warning, it just vanishes from the resolved config (while `args` is accepted). Unknown-key validation would have surfaced this.

**Asks:** (a) stop hardcoding `--effort max`, or make it a default the config can override; (b) append agent `args` AFTER builtin flags so declar

title: Order-tracking wisps accumulate unbounded (250k+ rows) because `gc order sweep-tracking` prunes a trickle and aborts on orphaned rows — idle dolt pegged, ~85s session spawns
body:
**Environment:** gc 1.3.2, bd 1.0.5, dolt 2.1.10, macOS arm64, supervisor-managed single city, 2 rigs, ~284 real issues, default system order set.

**Problem.** The order machinery mints one tracking wisp (~6 events) per order run, continuously, at sub-minute cadence — normal by design. The reaper, `gc order sweep-tracking`, closes them fine but the **prune deletes only a trickle and is orphan-fragile**, so closed wisps accumulate without bound. Measured end state on an *idle* city: **wisps 35,198 / wisp_events 211,858 / wisp_labels 106,022** against 284 real issues (250k+ rows total); dolt at **90–110% of a core while idle**; `gc session new` pin→active **~85s**.

**Proof the rows are the driver (not disk, not user load):**
- `gc supervisor stop` → dolt CPU drops to **0%** (the load is gc's own order/query machinery).
- Bulk-purging the wisp rows (250k → ~250) → idle CPU **90%→34%**, spawn pin→active **~85s→~25–38s**.
- Pausing the only adopter-added order changed nothing (73%→85%, noise).

**The prune defect specifically:**
- One run deleted **137 of 35k**; another **2 of 63** — far below the mint rate.
- It **throws `delete bead: <id>: bead not found` on orphaned wisps** (rows whose wisp↔events↔deps integrity broke; we found ids present in *neither* `wisps` nor `issues`) and stalls. On clean data it runs error-free, so the abort is orphan-triggered — but the first orphan starts the snowball.

**Asks:** (a) make the prune orphan-tolerant (skip/repair, don't abort); (b) dele

title: Proposal: formula run profiling support
body:
## Summary

Running a formula today produces a result but no record of *how* the run spent its time. When a `build-from-requirements` run takes 3.5 hours, there is no supported way to answer "where did it go?" — the evidence is scattered across the city event log, session beads, provider transcripts, usage facts, reconciler traces, Dolt history, and git, each with its own retention policy.

The key architectural finding: **almost everything needed to profile a run already survives, durably, keyed by the workflow root bead id** — and packs can ship `gc` commands (`commands/<name>/run.sh`, convention-discovered by `internal/config/command_discovery.go:57`), event-triggered orders, formulas, and scripts. So this proposes profiling as a **pack first**:

- **v0 — a `profiler` pack, no core changes.** `gc profile collect <root>` assembles a complete, durable capture for *any* run — including runs that already happened and runs that crashed — from the durable sources. `gc profile report` renders the timing analysis; `gc profile compare` diffs two captures; a `bench-nullop` formula measures pure orchestration overhead; a `profile-analyze` formula + analyst role write the narrative interpretation. The pack profiles what the user's existing storage already holds — it deliberately implements no backup of run state or conversation logs.
- **Core enablers — a short, prioritized follow-up list** for the few things a pack provably cannot reach (durable spawn-phase timings, `RunID` filter p

title: singleton pool + same-template named_session: identity normalization self-collision spams log + writes store every reconcile pass
body:
## Problem

When an agent is declared **both** as a `min=0/max=1` pool (`[[agent]]`) **and** as a configured `[[named_session]]` for the same template, the controller spams a deferral log line **and** does a `beads.Update` (stamping `pool_alias_conflict{,_count,_at}`) on **every reconcile pass**, forever.

The singleton-pool identity normalizer tries to normalize its instance to the canonical (bare template) name, but that alias is permanently reserved by the agent's own configured named session (`ensureSessionAliasAvailable` → "reserved for configured named session"). The normalization can never succeed, so `normalizeNonExpandingPoolSessionBeadForSelection` takes the deferral branch every pass:

```
buildDesiredState: pool "st/support.intake-poller": deferring singleton pool identity normalization
for bead <id>: ... session alias already exists: "st/support.intake-poller" reserved for configured
named session st/support.intake-poller
```

Observed live: ~168–267 lines per run, `pool_alias_conflict_count` climbing into the hundreds. It's **non-fatal** (the session launches under its ephemeral name and processes work) but it is log spam **plus** a per-tick store write on every pass — the latter adds to idle controller store load (cf. #2463).

## Why it's benign

For a singleton (`max=1`), the only holder of the canonical alias is the agent's own named-session identity — which legitimately owns it (that's the identity #3766 wakes). So the "collision" is a self-collision, not a

title: doctor: rig-pack-coverage false positive for local pack replacements with same pack name
body:
In superlzy-city, `gc doctor` reports:

- `rig-pack-coverage - 1 rig-scoped named_session(s) not covered by rig imports`
- JSON detail: `pack "gastown" declares rig-scoped named_session "witness" (mode=always) - missing from rig(s): superlzy-dash, slc`

Current config intentionally imports the city-level remote `gastown` pack, while two rigs replace that pack with local copies:

- `superlzy-dash`: `[rigs.imports.gastown] source = "packs/gastown-dh"`
- `slc`: `[rigs.imports.gastown] source = "packs/gastown-slc"`

Both local copies have `[pack].name = "gastown"` and declare the same rig-scoped always witness session in `pack.toml`. They are deliberate replacements: `superlzy-dash` uses a distinct polecat namepool, and `slc` carries local prompt/formula changes plus its namepool. Replacing them with the remote pack just to satisfy doctor would remove intended behavior.

Likely root cause: `internal/doctor/checks_rig_coverage.go` iterates city `cfg.PackDirs` and calls `rigHasPackDir(c.cfg.RigPackDirs, rig.Name, packDir)`, which compares exact absolute pack directory paths. A rig-local replacement with the same pack name and equivalent required named_session declarations cannot satisfy that exact-dir comparison.

Expected behavior: count a rig as covered when it imports a pack with the same `[pack].name` that declares the required rig-scoped always named_session, or otherwise distinguish exact-pack-dir gaps from intentional same-name replacements and provide an accurate hint.

title: control-dispatcher --follow serve loop never quiesces: multi-fork bd ready scan up to 12x/min per dispatcher on a fully idle city
body:
## Problem

The control-dispatcher `--follow` serve loop's idle backoff caps at 5s (`workflowServeMaxIdleSleep`, rationale in-code: raw `bd` writes publish no city event, so the re-poll is the only way to notice those transitions). Each sweep runs the work query — a shell that forks several `bd --readonly --sandbox ready` subprocesses (one per identity candidate, plus two per routed target: `gc.run_target` + `gc.routed_to`).

On a **fully idle** city this never quiesces: every dispatcher pays a multi-fork `bd ready` scan up to ~12×/min, forever. On our 1-rig city (two dispatchers: city + rig) we measured ~50 serve trace events/min **per dispatcher** with the city otherwise quiescent — with the controller now reading in-process (native store), this idle serve polling is the dominant *residual* `bd`-subprocess producer behind #2463.

## Ask

A second backoff tier: after N consecutive empty sweeps (i.e. sustained proven quiet), extend the sleep cap (5s → ~30s). Any relevant event or non-empty drain already resets `idleSweeps` to 0, so multi-hop workflow latency is untouched; the only cost is a one-time ≤30s first-hop pickup for an event-less (raw `bd` write) transition arriving after a long quiet period.

Refs #2463 (this is one producer, not the whole issue).

title: feat(providers): first-class launch exec-wrapper for fs-sandboxing spawned agents (bwrap)
body:
## Summary

Add a **provider-level launch exec-wrapper** (e.g. `exec_prefix` / `wrapper` on `builtin:claude` and other runtimes) so operators can prepend a sandbox command (bubblewrap / `unshare`) to gc's normal, fully-resolved agent launch — *without* hand-replicating the invocation. This is the missing structural lever for **filesystem least-privilege on spawned agents**.

## Motivation — a real store-destruction incident

An unattended pool agent running under `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (correct for headless MCP work — it removes all Bash approval prompts) "diagnosed" its bd/Dolt connection errors by running:

```
rm -rf .beads/dolt/* && rm -rf st/.beads/dolt/* && bd bootstrap
```

This destroyed the managed root + rig Dolt data dirs and minted fresh project-ids → a project-identity split-brain across copies. Recovery took a full manual reconciliation.

Mitigations that are **not** enough on their own:
- **Harness `permissions.deny` for Bash** (`Bash(rm:*)`, `Bash(dolt:*)`, `Bash(bd bootstrap:*)`…): we verified it *is* honored even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, but it is **best-effort and trivially bypassable** — `find <path> -delete`, `/bin/rm`, `python -c 'shutil.rmtree(...)'`, heredoc scripts, etc. all evade command-prefix matching. A speed-bump, not a wall.
- **Prompt hardening** ("never self-repair infra"): reduces the *trigger* but is advisory.

The only real wall is **fs least-privilege**: the agent process must not be able to write/delete the manage

title: workspace-identity deprecation hint can silently break Discord (and other city.toml workspace.name consumers) if followed before pack pins catch up
body:
The v2 deprecation warning tells operators to move workspace identity out of `city.toml`:

```
city.toml: workspace identity fields are deprecated in v2; move them to .gc/site.toml (workspace.name); … (run `gc doctor --fix` if this is the root city.toml …)
```

Following it — by hand or via `gc doctor --fix` — is a trap for any city that pins a pack release which still resolves the supervisor scope from `city.toml` `workspace.name` only (gascity-packs discord before 26cfc61). With the declared name stripped, scope discovery comes back empty, delivery falls back to the legacy default API port, and **all inbound Discord messages die with connection refused — silently** (the gateway stays up; only per-message ingress receipts record the failures).

This isn't hypothetical: on one deployment the name was removed from a root `city.toml` during an unrelated edit, and inbound DMs were eaten for ~2 days with zero alarms before the receipts were checked.

Two asks, either/both:

1. **Caveat the hint** (doctor + config load warning): note that installed packs pinned before the site-binding-aware releases may still read `city.toml` `workspace.name`, so operators should update/re-pin those packs before stripping the field. A one-line addition to the warning text would have prevented the incident above.

title: gc doctor dolt-backup check should recognize external Dolt backup remotes
body:
Source: superlzy-city bead `slc-9vw`.

`gc doctor` v1.3.2 currently reports these warnings in a city whose rigs use an external Dolt accessory at `superlzy-dolt:3306`:

```text
rig:apicity:dolt-backup       rig "apicity": no dolt backup registered (expected /gc/.dolt-backup/ac)
rig:superlzy-dash:dolt-backup rig "superlzy-dash": no dolt backup registered (expected /gc/.dolt-backup/dh)
rig:slc:dolt-backup           rig "slc": no dolt backup registered (expected /gc/.dolt-backup/slc)
```

In this deployment the external Dolt accessory self-manages backups to DoltHub and the local Dolt-pack backup orders are intentionally disabled. Re-running local `DOLT_BACKUP('sync', ...)` against the external server is not the right remediation and has already timed out client-side in this city.

The current checker appears to register `DoltBackupCheck` for active managed bd-store rigs when `GC_DOLT != skip`, but the check only accepts these local signals:

- populated `<city>/.dolt-backup/<db>` directory
- backup entry in `<managed-dolt-data-dir>/<db>/.dolt/repo_state.json`

For an external SQL-server endpoint, the authoritative backup remotes live on the external Dolt server, not in the local managed data dir. The fix should make the doctor path external-endpoint aware: either query registered backup remotes from the external Dolt server with a bounded probe, or explicitly skip/degrade the local backup registration warning when the city/rig `dolt_host`/`dolt_port` points to an external endpo

title: Hook projection blind-appends the ubs PreToolUse hook every reconcile → unbounded .claude/settings.json bloat
body:
## Summary
The per-session config reconciler **appends** the `ubs` git-commit `PreToolUse` hook to each agent's `.claude/settings.json` on every reconcile tick **without deduplicating**, so `.hooks.PreToolUse` grows without bound on long-lived active sessions. The hook is projected (blind-append) rather than upserted.

## Evidence (observed 2026-06-25)
- `switchyard/crew/conductor` (active, 5 days old): `.hooks.PreToolUse` reached **5,760 identical entries / 1.4 MB** (was 2,212 a few minutes earlier — actively climbing).
- `wherigo/crew/compass` (active): **1,810 entries / 459 KB**, plus a 9.5 MB `.bak-bloat` from a prior manual cleanup (i.e. it recurs).
- An active polecat worktree: 419 entries. Fresh/idle agents: exactly **1** (the healthy baseline).

All duplicates are byte-identical:
```
if echo "$TOOL_INPUT" | grep -q 'git commit'; then ubs --staged --format=json 2>/dev/null || true; fi
```

## Regrowth rate (repro)
After manually deduping to 1 entry, ~20–40s later on **active** sessions: `conductor` 1→6, `compass` 1→4; an **idle** worktree stayed at 1. Regrowth correlates with session *liveness* (~1 entry every few seconds), which rules out "once at session start" and points at the per-tick reconcile/projection loop.

## Impact
- Every `Bash` tool call evaluates N `PreToolUse` matchers (perf drag that scales with the bloat).
- A single `git commit` fires `ubs --staged` N times (thousands, for long-lived crews).
- Multi-MB `settings.json` parsed on every session start; r
